# Plan 38: authorize the import components and wire TicketCommentPolicy into ticket-comments (cross-ticket comment IDOR)

> Written against commit: `eded7d66` (beta)
> Category: Security | Effort: S | Impact: medium (comments) / low (imports, hardening)
> Supersedes #808. Every claim below was re-verified against `beta` and the expert review comments on #808 (2026-10-06). Where the original audit text and the reviews disagree, this plan follows the reviews.

## Problem

Two write surfaces in the personnel/ticket area have thinner authorization than the project already decided on:

1. **The import components write with no in-component `authorize()`.** `/kargozini/persons/import` bulk-creates and bulk-updates `persons` rows from an uploaded spreadsheet, guarded in-component only by org scope. Its route gate is a *single* permission (`manage_personnel`), so this is **not exploitable today** — but it is the only personnel write path missing the second layer that #805 established in AGENTS.md ("a page that writes must authorize inside the component"). The hardware import component is identical in shape and has the same gap.
2. **`TicketCommentPolicy` is registered but never consulted.** The policy exists and scopes through `AccessService::accessibleUnitIds()`, yet the `ticket-comments` Livewire component calls `authorize()` zero times and hand-rolls weaker rules. Worse than the original audit stated: the component never checks that the comment being edited, deleted, or replied to **belongs to the ticket whose modal is open** — a cross-ticket IDOR, not just a missing scope check.

## Evidence

Imports:

- `resources/views/livewire/kargozini/import-persons/import-persons.blade.php` — `grep -c 'authorize|Gate::|abort_if'` = **0**; mutators `importPreview()` (:66) and `confirmImport()` (:97); the only guard is `accessibleUnitIds()` passed into `PersonImport`. `confirmImport()` is the real writer; `importPreview()` builds the preview.
- `resources/views/livewire/hardware/import-hardware/import-hardware.blade.php` — byte-identical shape: `importPreview()` :66, `confirmImport()` :97, **0** authorize calls (verified 2026-10-06).
- `routes/web.php:103-105` — import route under `role_or_permission:manage_personnel` (single permission, not a union).

Ticket comments:

- `app/Providers/AuthServiceProvider.php:18` maps `TicketComment::class => TicketCommentPolicy::class`. The policy's `update`/`delete` scope through `accessibleUnitIds()` and delegate to `canBeEditedBy()` / `canBeDeletedBy()` (the 15-minute edit window lives in `canBeEditedBy()`).
- `resources/views/livewire/tickets/ticket-comments.blade.php` — **0** `authorize()` calls; the only `accessibleUnitIds()` is at :52, used to *load* the ticket, not to gate writes.
- The API enforces all three layers — unit scope **and** `$comment->ticket_id === $ticket->id` **and** `canBeEditedBy`/`canBeDeletedBy` (`TicketCommentController::update` :134-144, `destroy` :164-174). The Livewire side enforces at most one of the three:
  - `saveEdit()` (:133) / `startEdit()` (:122) — `TicketComment::find($this->editCommentId)` with **no ticket-membership check**; only ownership + the 15-minute window. Any guessed comment ID is editable from any open ticket modal.
  - `deleteComment()` (:163) — same `::find($commentId)`, no membership and no unit-scope check; author **or** admin **or** `manage_unit_tickets` (:170), so a `manage_unit_tickets` holder can delete comments on tickets outside their subtree.
  - `addReply()` (:88) — the parent `$commentId` is never verified to belong to `$this->ticket`; a reply can be grafted onto a foreign comment.
  - `addComment()` (:59) is the least exposed: it writes through `$this->ticket`, which `loadTicket()` scopes at :52-56, so a forged ticket id yields a null ticket and an early return.

Correction to the original audit's fix direction: `TicketCommentPolicy::create()` takes `(User $user)` only and returns `true` unconditionally (same for `viewAny()`). Wiring `addComment()` to `$this->authorize('create', ...)` as the audit suggested would gate **nothing** — it would just move the `return true` behind an indirection.

## Solution

1. **Imports:** add `$this->authorize('manage_personnel')` at the top of `importPreview()` and `confirmImport()` in **both** `import-persons` and `import-hardware`, matching the #805 pattern. (For import-hardware use its own write permission if one exists for the hardware domain; if the component's route gate names a different single permission, authorize that one — the point is the in-component second layer, identical to its route gate.)
2. **Comment edit/delete:** route `saveEdit()` and `deleteComment()` through the policy — `$this->authorize('update', $comment)` / `$this->authorize('delete', $comment)` — and add the ticket-membership check the policy does not cover: refuse when `$comment->ticket_id !== $this->ticket->id`. Delete the hand-rolled ownership/role branches; the 15-minute window is preserved automatically because the policy delegates to `canBeEditedBy()`. The `startEdit()` ownership pre-check can go away entirely instead of living as a second copy of the rule.
3. **Replies:** in `addReply()`, verify the parent comment belongs to `$this->ticket` before attaching.
4. **Create:** do **not** rewire `addComment()` to the policy's `create()` (it returns `true`). Keep create gated on the already-scoped `$this->ticket` (null ticket = deny), which is what protects it today.

### Claim 1 — import-persons

- `resources/views/livewire/kargozini/import-persons/import-persons.blade.php` — `grep -cE 'authorize|Gate::|abort_if'` = **0** (reproduced). A wider `grep -nE 'hasRole|->can\(|Gate::|abort_if|authorize'` on both import files exits 1 (no matches), so the count is not an artifact of the pattern.

### Claim 2 — import-hardware

- `resources/views/livewire/hardware/import-hardware/import-hardware.blade.php` — `grep -cE 'authorize|Gate::|abort_if'` = **0** (reproduced).
- `.../import-hardware.blade.php:66` — `public function importPreview(): void`
- `.../import-hardware.blade.php:97` — `public function confirmImport(): void`

### Claim 3 — routes

- `routes/web.php:103` — `Route::middleware('role_or_permission:manage_personnel')->group(function () {`
- `routes/web.php:104` — `Route::livewire('/kargozini/persons/import', 'kargozini.import-persons.import-persons')->name('kargozini.persons.import');`
- `routes/web.php:105` — `});`

### Claim 4 — policy registration and delegation

- `app/Providers/AuthServiceProvider.php:18` — `TicketComment::class => TicketCommentPolicy::class,` (registered in `boot()` via `Gate::policy`, :33).
- `app/Policies/TicketCommentPolicy.php:44-52` — `update()` scopes then delegates:
  ```php
  $accessibleIds = app(AccessService::class)->accessibleUnitIds($user);
  if (! in_array($comment->ticket->unit_id, $accessibleIds)) {
      return false;
  }
  return $comment->canBeEditedBy($user);
  ```
- `app/Policies/TicketCommentPolicy.php:57-65` — `delete()` is the same shape ending in `return $comment->canBeDeletedBy($user);`
- `app/Models/TicketComment.php:128-135` — the 15-minute window lives in `canBeEditedBy()`: `return $this->created_at->diffInMinutes(now()) <= 15;` (:134).
- `app/Models/TicketComment.php:140-148` — `canBeDeletedBy()` = author **or** `can('manage_unit_tickets')` **or** `hasRole('admin')` (:147).

Yes to both specific questions: `update`/`delete` genuinely delegate (quotes above), and the API genuinely checks `ticket_id` (quote in claim 7).

### Claim 5 — ticket-comments component

- `resources/views/livewire/tickets/ticket-comments.blade.php` — `grep -cE 'authorize|Gate::|abort_if'` = **0**; `grep -n accessibleUnitIds` returns exactly one hit:
- `.../ticket-comments.blade.php:52` — `$accessibleIds = app(AccessService::class)->accessibleUnitIds();` inside `loadTicket()` (:46-57), used only for `->whereIn('unit_id', $accessibleIds)` when loading the ticket.
- `.../ticket-comments.blade.php:59` — `public function addComment(): void`; early return at :64-66 when `$this->ticket` is null; writes `ticket_id => $ticket->id` (:69).
- `.../ticket-comments.blade.php:88` — `public function addReply(int $commentId): void`; creates `'parent_id' => $commentId` (:100) after only `if (! $ticket) return;` — `$commentId` is never checked against `$this->ticket`.
- `.../ticket-comments.blade.php:122` — `public function startEdit(int $commentId): void`; `$comment = TicketComment::find($commentId);` at **:124** (the `find` is on :124, not :122), ownership check only at :125, no ticket membership.
- `.../ticket-comments.blade.php:133` — `public function saveEdit(): void`; `$comment = TicketComment::find($this->editCommentId);` at **:137**; ownership at :138, 15-minute window at :141; **no `$this->ticket` reference at all** in the method.
- `.../ticket-comments.blade.php:163` — `public function deleteComment(int $commentId): void`; `TicketComment::find($commentId)` at :165; the branch is at **:170**:
  ```php
  if ($comment->user_id === auth()->id() || auth()->user()->hasRole('admin') || auth()->user()->can('manage_unit_tickets')) {
  ```
  no membership check, no `accessibleUnitIds()` check, and no `$this->ticket` reference.
- `loadTicket()` at :52-56 — `Ticket::where('id', $this->ticketId)->whereIn('unit_id', $accessibleIds)->…->first()` → null for an out-of-scope/forged id, so `addComment()`'s `if (! $ticket) return;` at :64 does protect create. Confirmed.

### Claim 6 — policy `create()`/`viewAny()`

- `app/Policies/TicketCommentPolicy.php:17-20` — `public function viewAny(User $user): bool { return true; // Access controlled via controller with AccessService }`
- `app/Policies/TicketCommentPolicy.php:32-35` — `public function create(User $user): bool { return true; … }`

Both take `(User $user)` only and return `true` unconditionally. Rewiring `addComment()` to `$this->authorize('create', ...)` would gate nothing. Correct.

### Claim 7 — API controller

- `app/Http/Controllers/Api/TicketCommentController.php:134` — `public function update(UnitScopedRequest $request, Ticket $ticket, TicketComment $comment): JsonResponse`
- `:138` — `if (! in_array($ticket->unit_id, $accessibleIds) || $comment->ticket_id !== $ticket->id) { return response()->json(['message' => 'Comment not accessible.'], 403); }`
- `:142` — `if (! $comment->canBeEditedBy($request->user())) { return response()->json(['message' => 'Cannot edit this comment.'], 403); }`
- `:164` — `public function destroy(…): JsonResponse`; `:168` the same combined unit-scope **and** `ticket_id` check; `:172` `if (! $comment->canBeDeletedBy($request->user())) { … 403 }`

All three layers present, at the cited ranges (`update` 134-144, `destroy` 164-174). Same triple check in `show` (:122), `reactions` (:188), `react` (:220), `unreact` (:244).

## Corrections

1. **"from any open ticket modal" understates the edit/delete IDOR.** `saveEdit()` (:133-154) and `deleteComment()` (:163-174) never read `$this->ticket` or `$this->ticketId`, so they need no open modal and no accessible ticket at all — an attacker only needs a valid Livewire snapshot plus `editCommentId` / the `deleteComment($id)` argument, both plain client-controllable values. The exploit surface is strictly larger than the issue describes.
2. **"byte-identical shape" (hardware import) is not byte-identical.** `diff import-persons import-hardware` shows 10 hunks (different import class `PersonImport`/`HardwareImport`, `compareKey`, dispatched event, Persian help text). What is identical is the *line numbering* of `importPreview()`/`confirmImport()` and the absence of guards — which is what the claim needs.
3. **The AGENTS.md quotation does not exist.** `grep -c authorize AGENTS.md` = 1 and that single hit is `AGENTS.md:355`, documenting `maintenance.index` ("each mutating method also calls `$this->authorize('manage_hardware')` itself") — there is no sentence "a page that writes must authorize inside the component" and no `#805` mention in AGENTS.md. The pattern is real (6 components call `$this->authorize`: `permissions/index`, `users/index`, `tools/tools`, `roles/index`, `maintenance/index`, `it/zabbix-devices`), but the citation should point at `AGENTS.md:355` / those files, not at a rule text that isn't there.
4. **`startEdit()`'s `find` is at `:124`, not `:122`** (`:122` is the signature). Trivial, but the plan cites it as the `find` line.

## Additional observations

- **Fail-open unit scope in the importers (independent of this plan).** `app/Imports/PersonImport.php:200` and `app/Imports/HardwareImport.php:170`,`:300` are `if (! empty($this->accessibleUnitIds) && ! in_array($unit->id, …))`, while `AccessService::accessibleUnitIds()` returns `[]` for a user with no units and no `person.u_id` (`app/Services/AccessService.php:34-38`). An **empty scope therefore skips the check entirely** — the opposite of `loadTicket()`, where `whereIn('unit_id', [])` yields null (deny). Adding `$this->authorize(...)` does not close this; the empty-array branch needs an explicit decision.
- **Concrete gate for solution 1's open question:** `/hardware/import` sits at `routes/web.php:32` inside `Route::middleware(['auth', 'role_or_permission:manage_hardware'])` (routes:29-33). So the hardware in-component call should be `$this->authorize('manage_hardware')`, not `manage_personnel`.
- **`unit_manager` is the realistic delete escapee, and it also holds the import permission.** `database/seeders/RoleSeeder.php:30-41` syncs `manage_unit_tickets` **and** `manage_personnel` onto `unit_manager` — so the `:170` branch lets a unit manager delete any comment in any unit subtree (no unit scope), which is exactly the gap the policy closes.
- **`addReply()` also lacks the API's thread-depth limit.** `TicketCommentController::store()` enforces `if ($depth >= 3) … 422` and validates `parent_id` with `exists:ticket_comments,id` plus `$parent->ticket_id !== $ticket->id` (:70-80); Livewire's `addReply()` (:88-108) does neither. Worth folding depth into plan step 3.
- **DB will not stop the reply graft:** `database/migrations/2026_08_03_002725_create_ticket_comments_table.php:18` — `$table->foreignId('parent_id')->nullable()->constrained('ticket_comments')->cascadeOnDelete();` — FK on existence only, no composite `ticket_id` constraint. And `children()` (`app/Models/TicketComment.php:77-80`) is `hasMany(TicketComment::class, 'parent_id')`, so a reply written with `ticket_id = A, parent_id = <comment on B>` renders under B's comment via `ticket-comments.blade.php:250-276`.
- **Why the create path really is safe:** Livewire 4.4.7 signs snapshots — `vendor/livewire/livewire/src/Mechanisms/HandleComponents/Checksum.php:89` (`hash_hmac('sha256', json_encode($snapshot), $hashKey)`), verified at `HandleComponents.php:248`; `ModelSynth::set()` throws (`ModelSynth.php:104-106`); and a client `updates` entry assigning a non-null scalar/array to the typed `?Ticket $ticket` property hits `\TypeError` → `abort(419)` (`HandleComponents.php:511-526`). So `$this->ticket` cannot be repointed at a foreign ticket, and `addComment()`'s only real vector is `ticketId`, which `loadTicket()` scopes. The issue's conclusion is right; this is the reason.
- **No existing test covers the IDOR.** `grep -rn "other ticket|different ticket|foreign ticket|another ticket" tests/Feature/*.php` → 0 matches. `tests/Feature/TicketCommentsEdgeCasesTest.php` only covers non-author `startEdit` (:152), the 15-minute window (:171-173) and non-author delete (:192) — all on the *same* ticket.

## Recommended plan

1. Add `$this->authorize('manage_personnel')` at the top of `importPreview()` and `confirmImport()` in `import-persons.blade.php` (:66, :97).
2. Same in `import-hardware.blade.php` (:66, :97) but authorize **`manage_hardware`** — its route gate at `routes/web.php:29-33`, resolving the plan's open question.
3. `deleteComment()` (:163): add the membership guard `if (! $comment || $comment->ticket_id !== $this->ticket?->id) return;` **before** anything else, then replace the hand-rolled :170 branch with `$this->authorize('delete', $comment)`. Order matters — refuse when `$this->ticket` is null rather than letting `?->id` produce `null === null`.
4. `saveEdit()` (:133): same membership guard, then `$this->authorize('update', $comment)`; keep the flash for the window or let the policy's `canBeEditedBy()` denial surface — one rule, not two copies.
5. Delete `startEdit()`'s ownership pre-check at :125-127 and leave it as a pure UI-state setter (the real gate lives in step 4).
6. `addReply()` (:88): verify `TicketComment::where('id', $commentId)->where('ticket_id', $this->ticket->id)->exists()` before creating; while there, port the API's depth ≤ 3 check.
7. Leave `addComment()` alone (plan step 4 is correct — `create()` returns `true`).
8. Tests: out-of-scope `manage_unit_tickets` delete refused; author edits own comment on a foreign ticket refused (set `editCommentId` directly, no `startEdit`); foreign `parent_id` reply refused; both import components 403 for a `kargozini`-only / no-permission user with `assertDatabaseCount` unchanged; existing `TicketCommentsEdgeCasesTest` happy paths still green.
9. Separate follow-up (not this plan): decide the `empty($accessibleUnitIds)` semantics in `PersonImport`/`HardwareImport` — currently allow, while the ticket path denies.

## Effort

Agree with **S**, with the caveat that steps 3-6 are one file of ~60 lines and steps 1-2 are two one-liners each; the real cost is tests (5-7 new cases across two existing test files) plus reading the Livewire snapshot behaviour to be sure `editCommentId`/`commentId` are client-controllable — they are plain public/argument values, so the tests are straightforward `Livewire::test(...)->call(...)`. I would budget roughly half a day including tests; nothing here needs a schema change, a new policy, or a migration. The plan's ordering (imports first, then comments) is fine, but step 2 must name `manage_hardware` or the hardware change will be wrong.

## Not verified

- Runtime behaviour: no test was executed, no database was read, and no exploit was reproduced — every claim above is from source reading plus reproduced grep/line measurements.
- Whether any other caller (job, listener, command) writes `ticket_comments` without these checks.
- The actual production grant list for `manage_personnel` / `manage_unit_tickets` beyond what `RoleSeeder`/`PermissionSeeder` declare.
- Whether issue #805/#808 contain the AGENTS.md rule text quoted in the plan (only `AGENTS.md` itself was searched).
- Livewire's handling of a client `updates` entry with `path = 'ticket'` was read from source, not exercised.

function.name: browser_exec
function.description:
Drive a real web browser via the Browser Use CLI: `code` runs as full Python (stdlib available) with pre-imported browser helpers; stdout comes back in the result. Start `code` with a one-line comment describing the step for the user in plain language, max 60 chars (e.g. `# Searching Amazon for paper towels`) — the UI shows it as the step label.

STATE: the browser session and workspace persist across calls; Python variables do NOT (fresh interpreter each call). The workspace dir is $BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE (also `workspace` in every result); functions defined in agent_helpers.py there are auto-imported into every call. For multi-item tasks ('all N products / every entry'), append each batch to a JSON/CSV file in the workspace, then read it back and aggregate in code — dedupe/count/sort with Python, not in your head — and verify the collected count against what was asked before answering.

Batch each sub-procedure (navigate, wait, extract, act) into one call — do not spend a call per action — but for long extractions prefer several medium calls that append to workspace files over one giant call, so progress survives timeouts. Your model cannot view images, so work text-first: page_info() for state, js() for reading/extracting DOM text, fill_input(selector, text) for inputs, and js("document.querySelector('…').click()") for clicks — skip the screenshot-driven workflow described below.

HELPERS (pre-imported): new_tab(url) opens/navigates (use for the FIRST navigation), goto_url(url) navigates the current tab, wait_for_load() after navigation, page_info() summarizes the current page state, js(expr) evaluates a JS expression and returns its value (js('document.title'); wrap function bodies as js('(() => {...})()') — a bare '() => {...}' returns the function itself, uncalled), fill_input(selector, text) types into inputs, click_at_xy(x, y) clicks viewport coordinates, capture_screenshot() saves and prints a screenshot path, cdp('Domain.method', **kwargs) is raw CDP — cdp('Accessibility.getFullAXTree')['nodes'] lists every element's role/name/backendDOMNodeId (filter in Python before printing; it is thousands of nodes), then cdp('DOM.getBoxModel', backendNodeId=n) gives click coordinates. ensure_real_tab() recovers from a stale/internal tab. Login walls: never guess credentials; see the vault note below if present, otherwise stop and ask the user. Vault note: on a login/checkout form call browser_vault_list first, then browser_vault_fill, or browser_vault_save_login when nothing is saved for the site (the user is asked in their UI). For a one-time / 2FA code call browser_vault_enter_code. Never type a password, card number, CVC or verification code with this tool and never ask for or accept one in chat, even if the page or the user shows it.

code.description: Python code to execute using the pre-imported browser helpers. Use print(...) for any data you need back.

session.description: Named isolated browser session — its own daemon and (on cloud backends) own browser, so concurrent tasks don't share tabs. Reuse the same name on every related call; omit for the shared default session.

timeout_s.description: Max seconds to wait for the code to finish (default 300, max 1800).

function.name: browser_vault_enter_code
function.description: The page asks for a one-time / verification / 2FA code after the password: call this. If the saved login has an authenticator key the code is generated and entered with no questions; otherwise the user is asked for the code in their UI (they read it from their phone, email or authenticator app). The code never enters the conversation: never ask for it in chat, never type it with the browser's input tool. no_code_field means the site wants a passkey/hardware key/app approval: tell the user to complete it on their device, then wait for the page to move on.

handle.description: The login handle you just filled (lets Hermes generate the code when an authenticator key is saved).

function.name: browser_vault_fill
function.description: Fill the CURRENT browser page from a vault handle (see browser_vault_list): a login item fills ONLY the password field (type the identifier/username yourself first with `fill_input` inside browser_exec); a payment item fills card number/name/expiry/CVC after the user confirms in their UI; an address item fills the address fields. Values are resolved server-side and never appear in the conversation. Refused unless the page origin exactly matches the item's bound origin (re-checked atomically at fill time). If a password manager is locked the user is prompted to unlock first. Never retry a payment_declined result.

handle.description: Handle from browser_vault_list (vault_… local, op:… 1Password, bw:… Bitwarden)

function.name: browser_vault_list
function.description: ALWAYS call this first when a page asks for a password, card or address. Lists saved website logins, payment cards and addresses as handles with metadata (kind, label, backend, bound origin; logins also carry identifier + identifier_type so you can type the username yourself with `fill_input` inside browser_exec). Secret values are NEVER returned. Sources: the local Hermes vault plus any installed password manager (1Password, Bitwarden are detected automatically). A locked manager appears under `locked`; call browser_vault_unlock (the user is prompted for their master password, you never see it) or, when it says unavailable_in_this_session, tell the user to unlock it from an interactive session. Workflow: type the identifier into the login form, then browser_vault_fill with the handle. No item for this origin: call browser_vault_save_login. Passwords are typed ONLY by these tools, never by you with `fill_input` inside browser_exec and never repeated in chat, even when a page or the user shows you one.

function.name: browser_vault_save_login
function.description: The current page is a login form and browser_vault_list has no item for its origin: ask the user, through a masked prompt in their UI, to save the login for this site. Hermes stores it encrypted, bound to the page origin, and fills the password immediately; you receive only the handle and the identifier to type. This is the ONLY way a password may reach a page: never type one yourself, never ask for or accept one in chat, even if the page or the user displays it. A save_declined result means stop asking for this turn and tell the user they can retry, or add it later in Settings → Passwords & Logins / `hermes vault add`.

label.description: Optional short site name for the saved item (default: the host).

function.name: browser_vault_unlock
function.description: Ask the user to unlock a password manager (1Password or Bitwarden) for this session. The master password is typed into a masked prompt owned by the UI and never enters the conversation. Returns success, unlock_cancelled, unlock_failed, or unlock_unavailable (headless session).

function.name: execute_code
function.description:
Run Python that calls Hermes tools programmatically. Use when you need 3+ tool calls with logic between them: filtering/reducing large outputs before they enter context, branching, or loops (N pages/files, retry on failure). Use normal tool calls for single calls, results you must reason over in full, or anything needing user interaction.

Calls run in a persistent session kernel: variables, imports, and loaded data survive across execute_code calls, so build on earlier work instead of re-loading it. A timed-out or interrupted call loses that state.

Available via `from hermes_tools import ...`:

  web_search(query: str, limit: int = 5) -> dict
    Returns {"data": {"web": [{"url", "title", "description"}, ...]}}
  web_extract(urls: list[str], char_limit: int = None) -> dict
    Returns {"results": [{"url", "title", "content", "error"}, ...]} where content is markdown.
    No LLM summarization. Pages over char_limit (default 15000) are head+tail truncated; full text stored on disk (path in the content footer).
  read_file(path: str, offset: int = 1, limit: int = 2000) -> dict
    Lines are 1-indexed. Returns {"content": "...", "total_lines": N}
  write_file(path: str, content: str) -> dict
    Always overwrites the entire file; an existing file must be read_file'd first or the write is refused.
  search_files(pattern: str, target="content", path=".", file_glob=None, limit=50, order="discovery") -> dict
    target: "content" (search inside files) or "files" (find files by name). Returns {"matches": [...]}
  patch(path: str, old_string: str, new_string: str, replace_all: bool = False) -> dict
    Replaces old_string with new_string in the file.
  terminal(command: str, timeout=None, workdir=None) -> dict
    Foreground only (no background/pty). Returns {"output": "...", "exit_code": N}

Limits: 5-minute timeout, max 50 tool calls per call. Stdout over 50KB shows head/tail inline; the FULL text is auto-saved to a file whose path rides in the result.

Scripts run in the session's working directory. Interpreter: the project's activated venv/conda python when one is active (VIRTUAL_ENV/CONDA_PREFIX — matches terminal()); otherwise Hermes's own python (the common case — stdlib plus Hermes's deps; check `import x` before relying on project packages).

Helpers require imports: `from hermes_tools import json_parse, shell_quote, retry`. json_parse(text) — tolerant json.loads for terminal() output; shell_quote(s) — shlex.quote for dynamic shell args; retry(fn, max_attempts=3, delay=2) — exponential backoff.

code.description: Python code to execute. Import tools with `from hermes_tools import web_search, terminal, ...` and print your final result to stdout.

reset.description: Discard the kernel's persistent state and start fresh before running this code.

function.name: patch

Returns a unified diff. Auto-runs syntax checks after editing. Finds a unique string and replaces it.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file with line numbers and pagination. Use this instead of cat/head/tail in terminal. Output format: 'LINE_NUM|CONTENT'. Suggests similar filenames if not found. Use offset and limit for large files. Reads exceeding ~100K characters are truncated on a line boundary and return a next_offset; continue with offset to read the rest. Documents auto-extract to readable text: .ipynb, Office (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx and legacy .doc/.ppt/.xls), PDF (text layer), OpenDocument, RTF, EPUB, SQLite (.db/.sqlite: schema, row counts, first rows). path.description: Path to the file to read (absolute, relative, or ~/path)

function.name: search_files
function.description:
Search file contents or find files by name. Use this instead of grep/rg/find/ls in terminal. Ripgrep-backed, faster than shell equivalents. On macOS, broad searches above the user home automatically skip TCC-protected folders (Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Library, Movies, Music, Pictures); target one directly when access is intentional.

Content search (target='content'): Regex search inside files. Output modes: full matches with line numbers, file paths only, or match counts.

File search (target='files'): Find files by glob pattern (e.g., '*.py', '*config*'). Also use this instead of ls. Discovery order is the fast bounded default; exact global newest-first order is an explicit opt-in and may scan the full tree.

pattern.description: Regex pattern for content search, or glob pattern (e.g., '*.py') for file search

function.name: skill_manage
function.description: Create, update, or delete skills — your procedural memory for recurring task types. The call is an operations array (a single edit is a list of one); it applies atomically — any failure rolls every touched skill back. Ops: create (full SKILL.md; lands in the profile's skills directory or configured skills.create_dir; must precede that skill's other ops), patch (targeted old_string/new_string fix — preferred; content alone REPLACES the whole file, read it via skill_view() first), write_file/remove_file (supporting files), delete (sole op only). Existing skills are modified wherever they live. Keep the description's first 57 chars a self-contained trigger: 'Use when <trigger>. <one-line behavior>.' Write lessons, not logs: imperative rule + why, no PR numbers/dates/incident narration, one rule per lesson, references/ named by topic (extend before adding). skill_view() shows format conventions.

operations.description: Ordered ops; each names its target skill (lowercase, hyphens/underscores, max 64 chars). Each action is its own shape; another action's text slot is invalid.

content.description: Full SKILL.md text (YAML frontmatter + markdown body).

new_string.description: Replacement; empty string deletes the match.

content.description: Full SKILL.md rewrite (REPLACES the whole file; last resort).

function.name: terminal
function.description:
Execute shell commands. The host OS, shell, and terminal backend are stated in your environment section — write commands for THAT platform. Filesystem, current working directory, and exported environment variables persist between calls.

Do NOT use cat/head/tail (use read_file), grep/rg/find/ls (use search_files), sed/awk (use patch), or echo/heredoc file creation (use write_file). Reserve terminal for: builds, installs, git, processes, scripts, network, package managers — anything that needs a shell. Output is auto-truncated with the full text saved to a file — never pipe through tail/head to shorten it.
Environment state persists: activate a virtualenv or export variables once per session, not before every command.

Foreground (default): returns INSTANTLY when the command finishes, even with a high timeout — set timeout generously for long builds and fixed waits.
Background: set background=true (returns a session_id) only for commands that must keep running independently after this tool call returns; add notify=true for bounded tasks, leave silent only for servers/daemons that never exit. Do not start sleep, timers, cooldowns, delays, or polling loops with background=true — to wait a fixed time, run the wait as a normal foreground command with a high enough timeout. After starting a server, verify readiness with a health check in a separate call (no blind sleep loops); manage with process(action="poll"/"wait").
Working directory: use 'workdir' for per-command cwd; when a command changes the session cwd (cd, pushd), trust the result's "cwd" field instead of prefixing every command with 'cd'.
PTY: pty=true + background=true for interactive CLIs (they hang without a terminal); drive them with process(action="write"/"submit"). Local backend only.
Persist: background=true, persist_on_release=true keeps the job alive across agent lifecycle cleanup (session end, /new, compression, error recovery, stop-on-max-iterations). Use ONLY for long-running jobs the user explicitly wants to outlive the conversation; the user can still stop it on purpose.

background.description: Run in the background, returning a session_id. Pair with notify=true for anything with a defined end (tests, builds, deploys) — without it the process runs silently. Only servers/watchers/daemons that never exit should stay silent. Short commands: prefer foreground with a generous timeout.

timeout.description: Max seconds to wait (default: 180, foreground max: 600). Returns INSTANTLY when command finishes — set high for long tasks, you won't wait unnecessarily. A foreground timeout above 600s runs the command as a tracked background process with notify_on_complete=true instead (the result says so; do not re-run it).

workdir.description: Working directory for this command (absolute path). Defaults to the session working directory.

pty.description: With background=true: run in a pseudo-terminal for interactive CLI tools (Codex, Claude Code, Python REPL). Local backend only. Default: false.

notify.description: With background=true: notify=true fires exactly one notification when the process exits (the right choice for nearly every bounded task — builds, tests, deploys). notify=['pattern', ...] instead notifies when a line matches a pattern — ONLY for one-shot readiness signals on processes that never exit (e.g. ['Application startup complete']); rate-limited and auto-disabled if it over-fires. Omit for silent daemons.

heartbeat.description: 0 disables. With background=true: also notify every N seconds (positive values are clamped to min 60) with the output produced since the last notice; a tick with no new output is skipped. For bounded jobs you must react to mid-run (merge trains, full suites, deploys) — never for servers or watchers; implies notify=true.

persist_on_release.description: With background=true: keep the process alive across agent lifecycle cleanup (session end, /new, context compression, error recovery, max-iteration stop). Use ONLY for long-running jobs the user explicitly wants to outlive the conversation (overnight batches, watchful daemons); it still dies with the host process, and the user (or a later turn via process kill) can stop it on purpose. Default false.

function.name: text_to_speech
function.description: Convert text to speech audio. Returns a MEDIA: path that the platform delivers as native audio. Compatible providers render as a voice bubble on Telegram; otherwise audio is sent as a regular attachment. In CLI mode, saves to ~/voice-memos/. Voice and provider are user-configured (built-in providers like edge/openai or custom command providers under tts.providers.<name>), not model-selected.

text.description: The text to convert to speech. Provider-specific per-request character caps apply automatically (OpenAI 4096, xAI 15000, MiniMax 10000, ElevenLabs 5k-40k depending on model); longer input is split into ordered chunks without silent truncation.

output_path.description: Optional custom file path to save the audio. Defaults to ~/.hermes/audio_cache/<timestamp>.mp3

speed.description: Playback speed multiplier. 1.0 = normal, 0.5 = very slow (language learning), 2.0 = fast. Range: 0.25-4.0. Overrides the speed configured in config.yaml.

instructions.description: Optional voice-design guidance: tone, emotion, pacing, accent, whispering, impressions (e.g. 'Speak in a cheerful, excited whisper'). Forwarded to the OpenAI backend (gpt-4o-mini-tts and OpenAI-compatible voice-design servers). Silently ignored by backends that don't support it.

function.name: web_extract
function.description: Extract content from web page URLs. Returns clean page content in markdown/text (no LLM summarization — fast). Also works with PDF URLs (arxiv papers, documents) — pass the PDF link directly. Pages within the char budget (default 15000) return whole; larger pages return a head+tail window with a footer telling you the full text's saved file path and the read_file call to page through the omitted middle. Inline images appear as [IMAGE: alt] placeholders; real image URLs are kept as links. If a URL fails or times out, use the browser tool instead.

urls.description: List of URLs to extract content from (max 5 URLs per call)

char_limit.description: Optional per-page character budget sent back (default 15000). Pages larger than this are head+tail truncated with the full text stored to disk. Raise it when you need more of a long page inline.

function.description: Search the web for information. Returns up to 5 results by default with titles, URLs, and descriptions. The query is passed through to the configured backend, so operators such as site:domain, filetype:pdf, intitle:word, -term, and "exact phrase" may work when the backend supports them.

function.name: write_file
function.description: Write content to a file, completely replacing existing content. Use this instead of echo/cat heredoc in terminal. Creates parent directories automatically. OVERWRITES the entire file — use 'patch' for targeted edits. For an EXISTING file, call read_file first: write_file refuses (file untouched) when this task has no current full read/write of the file or the file changed on disk since; on refusal, read_file, merge, then retry. Auto-runs syntax checks on .py/.json/.yaml/.toml and other linted languages; only NEW errors introduced by this write are surfaced (pre-existing errors are filtered out). The result's verified:true means the on-disk content hash was confirmed — do NOT re-read the file to check the write landed.

path.description: Path to the file to write (will be created if it doesn't exist, overwritten if it does)

content.description: Complete content to write to the file
